title: 1975 AHSME Problem 26
statement: In acute triangle \(ABC\) the bisector of \(\angle A\) meets side \(BC\) at \(D.\) The circle with center \(B\) and radius \(BD\) intersects side \(AB\) at \(M;\) and the circle with center \(C\) and radius \(CD\) intersects side \(AC\) at \(N.\) Then it is always true that

solutions.text:
The angle bisector theorem gives \[ \frac{BD}{CD}=\frac{AB}{AC}. \] Since \(BM=BD\) and \(CN=CD,\) we have \(\frac{BM}{CN}=\frac{AB}{AC}.\) Therefore \(M\) and \(N\) divide \(AB\) and \(AC\) proportionally from \(B\) and \(C,\) so the converse of the side-splitter theorem gives \(MN\parallel BC.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Use \(BM=BD,\ CN=CD,\) and the angle bisector theorem
Show that \(\frac{BM}{CN}=\frac{AB}{AC}\) and apply the converse of the side-splitter theorem
